body.title: fix(orbit): show install hint instead of stale help when binary is missing
body.description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Running `glab orbit` before the binary is installed printed glab's own help, which listed commands the binary no longer has. It now says the Orbit CLI isn't installed and how to install it. If a custom binary path is set but broken, it names the path instead. The examples now cover only what glab handles itself, so they can't drift from the binary.

## Related issues

No project issue exists for this change.

## How has this been tested?

- `go test ./internal/commands/orbit/...`
- `golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=origin/main`
- `make gen-docs`



## Demo

Bare `glab orbit` with no binary installed, then `glab orbit --install --yes`, then the real Orbit help.

![glab orbit install hint and install](/uploads/fe953dde6da70af959eebda92c137d4d/demo-hold.svg)

<details>
<summary>Agent context</summary>

- `runHelp` prints to stdout through `LogInfof`. With no binary it shows the install hint (`glab orbit --install --yes`, `glab orbit --yes <command>`), using the spec's display name.
- If a custom path is set but invalid, it names the path plus `GLAB_ORBIT_CLI_BINARY_PATH` and the `orbit_cli_binary_path` key instead of suggesting `--install`.
- The `help` field on `options` is gone.
- `Example` is cut to `--install --yes`, `update`, `--yes skills get orbit` and `--help`.
- Tests cover a never-installed managed binary and a broken custom path. Docs regenerated.

</details>

body.title: feat(api): say how long to wait when glab api gets a 429
body.description:
## What

When `glab api` gets an HTTP 429, it now says how long to wait before retrying, after the usual error line:

```plaintext
glab: This endpoint has been requested too many times. Try again later. (HTTP 429)
glab: rate limited by search_rate_limit, retry after 1m0s
```

- The wait comes from `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP date), or else `RateLimit-Reset`.
- The limit's name comes from `RateLimit-Name`, when GitLab sends it.
- It applies to endpoint rate limits (JSON body) and Rack::Attack throttles (plain-text body), and to a later page that gets a 429 under `--paginate`.
- `glab api` still doesn't retry. The help text and docs now say so.

## Why

Most callers that hit a 429 from `glab api` resend the same request within seconds, before the rate-limit window resets, so most of the retries get another 429. With the hint, scripts and agents can wait the right amount.

It replaces !4259, which retried automatically. In https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8665#note_4217441683 we agreed that glab should fail fast on a 429 rather than wait, so the caller keeps control.

`RetryAfter` and `RateLimitHint` live in `internal/api` so the error handler for other commands can reuse them for #8665.

## Tests

- `internal/api`: header parsing, including an HTTP date, a fallback to `RateLimit-Reset`, and missing or unusable headers, plus the hint text.
- `glab api`: an endpoint-limit 429, a Rack::Attack 429, a 429 with no wait header, and a 429 on page 2 under `--paginate`.

Closes #8663

body.title: chore(lint): ignore testdata fixtures in markdownlint config
body.description:
## What does this MR do?

Adds `**/testdata/**` to `ignores` in `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`, with a comment saying why.

The `markdownlint` pre-push hook fails on unchanged `main` when lefthook lints every tracked file. That happens when `origin/HEAD` is missing, as on CI-style checkouts. Six test fixtures under `testdata` produce 11 errors (MD041, MD004, MD047). The fixtures are test inputs, not documentation, and fixing their lint errors could change what the tests read. So they are excluded rather than edited.

CI is unchanged. `check_docs_markdown` only lints `docs/**/*.md *.md`.

Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8746

## How to verify

This checkout has no `origin/HEAD`, which is the failing condition, so `git ls-files` stands in for lefthook's `{push_files}`:

```shell
git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 markdownlint-cli2
```

| markdownlint-cli2 | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 0.24.0 (`.tool-versions`) | 358 files, 11 issues in 6 files | 352 files, 0 issues |
| 0.23.2 (CI image version) | 358 files, 11 issues in 6 files | 352 files, 0 issues |

Passing files explicitly, as `{push_files}` does, honours the ignore: `markdownlint-cli2 internal/commands/snippet/create/testdata/file1.md test/testdata/README.md` lints 0 files.

## Other `{push_files}` hooks (Workplan step 4)

Run against all 364 tracked `*.md` files:

- `rumdl check --config docs/.rumdl/rumdl.toml`: passes, no issues. No follow-up is needed for `rumdl`.
- `lychee --offline --include-fragments`: **not verified**. The binary in this environment fails with `GLIBC_2.38/2.39 not found`. If it flags `testdata`, add a matching exclude in a follow-up rather than in this MR. The same applies to `go-lint`, which couldn't run in the local pre-push hook because another `golangci-lint` was already running. Neither is affected by this change.

## Readiness feedback

1. Verification reproduces the no-`origin/HEAD` path, with the 358 to 352 files and 11 to 0 issues counts from the issue.
2. `rumdl` is checked and clean. `lychee` couldn't be run, and the follow-up action is stated above.
3. Both markdownlint-cli2 0.24.0 and 0.23.2 were run and honour `ignores`.

No deviations from the Workplan. The optional `go test` sanity check was skipped, because no fixtures or Go code changed.

This file has CODEOWNERS, so approval is needed from the owners listed for `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`.

body.title: fix(df): evaluate nuget coordinates against the firewall API
body.description:
> [!note]
> :slot_machine: AI generated. This needs full human review.

## What does this MR do and why?

Maps `nuget` coordinates to the evaluate API's NuGet ecosystem, and lets `glab df package` accept `pkg:nuget/...` PURLs.

Without the mapping, `policy.ecosystemValue` returns `unsupported dependency firewall ecosystem "nuget"` for every NuGet coordinate, and the checker fails closed. A `.nupkg` download is then reported as blocked.

This matters for !4323. Its `DefaultMatchers` includes `NuGetMatcher`, so once it lands, a plain NuGet restore in a CI job is blocked with "policy check failed" and `ci-summary` exits 3. Duo raised this on !4323.

This is the first commit of !4180 (Ryan Wells), taken unchanged so it can land on its own. Git drops the duplicate when !4180 rebases.

## Testing

- `TestEcosystemValueMapsSupported/nuget` fails on `main` with `unsupported dependency firewall ecosystem "nuget"` and passes here. The `purl` tests cover parsing, and the `df package` tests cover the request for `pkg:nuget/Newtonsoft.Json@13.0.1`.
- `go test -race` passes for `internal/dependencyfirewall/...` and `internal/commands/df/...`. `golangci-lint` reports 0 issues and `make gen-docs` leaves no diff.
- Not run against a live firewall API.

## Not covered

Duo's other point on !4323, that NuGet's multipart PUT push path buffers any multipart PUT in a job, isn't addressed here.

## Related issues

Follow-up to !4323 and !4180. No separate issue.

body.title: Draft: [FixPipeline] https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/pipelines/3059455703
body.description:
`TestForwardsArgsAndRoutesThroughProxy` and the rest of the `dfcmd` package now pass. I ran `go test ./internal/commands/df/... ./internal/dependencyfirewall/...` without `-race`, because `-race` needs cgo and it wasn't enabled here. I did not run the full `make test-race`. **Cause:** the `cmdtest` factory hands out an empty `&gitlab.Client{}` by default. This MR's `pm.Run` now calls `policy.LoadSummary` whenever the client isn't nil, and that calls `client.BaseURL().Host`. On an empty client, `BaseURL()` dereferences nil. `TestEnvironmentHelp` failed because the panic took down the whole test binary, so I made no separate fix for it. **Fix:** I changed only the test file. It now has a small `newPolicyClient(t)` helper. The helper builds a real `*gitlab.Client` pointed at an `httptest` server that answers 404. The tests that run through `pm.Run` pass it with `cmdtest.WithGitLabClient(...)`. Because 404 is a real answer rather than "unreachable", `LoadSummary` returns nil and doesn't write to the user cache. I left `LoadSummary` unchanged. **`lint_commit`:** this job is not fixed, and no file change can fix it. It fails because the MR title starts with `POC:`. Rename the MR title to `feat(df): apply the policy's unreachable fallback when GitLab is down`. The pipeline stays red until then. **Files modified:** - `internal/commands/df/dfcmd/dfcmd_test.go` Fixes [failing pipeline](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/pipelines/3059455703)

body.title: revert: resolve the MR of a differently named local branch via tracking
body.description:
:robot: AI-generated

## What

Reverts !4309 (squash commit d3f8b51df28bda720eb99c74dfab7c4500b1fb43). After this MR, glab finds the MR for the current branch by the local branch name only, as it did before !4309.

## Why

`branch.<b>.merge` usually records the branch a local branch was created from, not the MR it belongs to. The fallback kept matching unrelated MRs, and every fix only closed one case:

- `git switch -c feat origin/main` matched any MR from `main` (fixed by allowing forks only).
- In a contributor clone (`origin` = fork), `git switch -c second-fix origin/main` matched the contributor's own fork MR from `main` (fixed by skipping the fork's default branch).
- Still open: a branch created from a non-default fork branch that has its own MR.

The same lookup is used by commands that change the MR (`close`, `merge`, `approve`, `delete`), so a wrong match acts on an unrelated MR. See the discussion in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4309#note_4215413983.

## Testing

Clean `git revert`. No later commits on `main` touch these files. `go build ./...`, the tests for `cmdutils`, `mr/...`, `git`, `testing` and `gen-docs`, and the lefthook pre-push checks pass.

body.title: fix(release): warn when notes and notes-file are both provided
body.description:
## Summary

- Warn on stderr when `glab release create` receives both `--notes` and `--notes-file`, instead of silently ignoring the file.
- Preserve the existing behavior: `--notes` wins, and the file is not opened.
- Clarify the flag precedence in the command help and the generated Markdown page.
- Add three command-level regression cases for both flags, `--notes` alone, and `--notes-file` alone.
